Maya: Daily finops snapshot — noticed ~28% jump in per-model token spend over the last 24h. Biggest delta is rwd-30b-q4 in eu-west-1. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood-inference/internal/finops/daily

Omar: Can you paste the per-route break? want to see if it's traffic skew or model-level ineff.

```
model,region,route,tokens,net_cost_usd
rwd-30b-q4,eu-west-1,/chat,45,520.34
rwd-30b-q4,us-west2,/assistant,12,138.90
```

Looks like /chat is the bulk in eu-west-1.

Li: FYI infra logs show autoscaler churn in dedicated-prod eu-west-1 yesterday 03:40-04:30 UTC — we had several scale-downs/ups and fallback to on-demand instances. That matches the time window. Example from autoscaler: `scaleDown -> 0 -> scaleUp 2 -> fallback:on-demand`

Theo: If dedicated pool dipped then on-demand cost + different kernel selection could spike per-token unit cost. Can we run a committed vs on-demand reconciliation for eu-west-1 last 24h? I can run the query.

Maya: please run it. Also I suspect a Canaries job hit prod. I saw a test job that targeted rwd-30b-q4 yesterday.

Omar: ran a quick agg, results look like: committed_gpu_hours=18, on_demand_gpu_hours=12, effective_unit_cost_per_1k_tokens = committed:0.008 / on-demand:0.023. So when we fell back we paid ~3x for those tokens.

finops-bot: ALERT: daily-burn threshold breached (24h spend > $40k). Rule: finops/daily-burn-alerts. See https://ops.redwood-inference/alerts/FD-349

Li: Confirmed — the load spike correlated with a Canary pipeline that didn't set the test tag. It was routed to the production model in eu-west-1. Ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-6421

Theo: Query snippet for committed vs on-demand breakdown (BigQuery):
```sql
SELECT region, model, SUM(tokens) as tokens, SUM(cost_usd) as cost, SUM(committed_cost_usd) as committed_cost
FROM `billing.model_token_usage`
WHERE timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 DAY)
GROUP BY region, model
ORDER BY cost DESC
```

Maya: Thanks. Action items:
- (Omar) confirm exact token ranges that hit on-demand (so we can websocket patch traffic fallback window)
- (Li) add block in Canary pipeline to enforce route:test header or explicit tag
- (Theo) add a per-model-per-route toggle in dashboard to show committed vs on-demand hours

Omar: On it. I already flipped a temporary scaling window to refuse scale-downs for 2h during peak windows. Patch: `infra autoscaler set min_replicas 2 --window 2h --region eu-west-1`

Li: I'll add the CI guard and update the runbook. Also tagging request: please make sure token-based requests include x-rwd-environment:test for test traffic.

Theo: I'll update the dashboard to include a per-model column for committed_hours and a filter for test vs prod tags. ETA: EOD.

Maya: Ok let's monitor tomorrow morning; for cost estimate shifting 12h of the affected tokens to dedicated would save roughly $9k/day based on Omar's numbers.
